Subject: Slot handback schedule + temporary autoscale threshold exception

Team —

Quick context: HealthSync (pilot customer) is asking for a predictable rotation of a 4-hour reserved slice nightly (UTC midnight-04:00) for the next three weeks while they run load-sensitive E2E tests. They also want a short-term increase to the autoscale upper threshold so their bursts don't get preempted mid-test.

We need to decide:
- whether we can schedule this as a nightly handback (slot rotation) without impacting mid-day production lanes,
- whether to grant a one-off autoscale upper threshold exception (and for how long), and
- what compensating controls (billing holdback, monitoring hooks, and preempt safety) we require.

My ask: Kimberley/Marcus — can you sketch capacity impact and whether ops can enforce a strict rotation window? Laura — can you advise on billing/contract implications for a three-week temporary carve?

Attachment: slot-handback-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal from Solutions with timeline and requested windows).

If we agree quickly we can lock this in before HealthSync's regression run on Friday.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Success 
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slot handback schedule + temporary autoscale threshold exception

Thanks Hannah — read the proposal. High level: doable but with caveats.

Summary of impact (quick numbers):
- Nightly 00:00-04:00 UTC reserved slice (p3.x8) will remove ~6% of our US west burst capacity during that window.
- If HealthSync's workload is spiky we should expect transient queueing for other pilots between 00:15-01:00 UTC based on historical tail patterns.

Options:
1) Strict handback window (recommended): enforce a hard reclaim at 04:00 with a 15-minute preempt notice; this minimizes ripple but risks aborting long-running test traces.
2) Soft handback with grace (alternate): extend to 04:30 if no queued prod traffic — lower risk to HealthSync but increases exposure to other tenants.

Autoscale threshold exception: I can authorize a one-week temporary increase to the upper autoscale threshold (+20% headroom) if we attach the following controls:
- Ops runbook change (temp) + two on-call hooks (ops + infra lead)
- Billing guardrail: provisional usage cap and manual approval if utilization exceeds 75% of the extra headroom
- HealthSync must run with a telemetry tag (customer:test-run) so we can filter spike signals

I uploaded a diff of the ops runbook with the exact trigger thresholds (ops-runbook-diff.txt). Marcus — can you confirm infra-level feasibility (kernel slots, evictions) and whether this will affect our canary SLA?

- Kim

Kimberly Park
Head of Product Operations

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

On Tue, Aug 4, 2026 at 11:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Autoscale threshold exception: I can authorize a one-week temporary increase to the upper autoscale threshold (+20% headroom) if we attach the following controls:
> - Ops runbook change (temp) + two on-call hooks (ops + infra lead)
> - Billing guardrail: provisional usage cap and manual approval if utilization exceeds 75% of the extra headroom
> - HealthSync must run with a telemetry tag (customer:test-run) so we can filter spike signals

All good. Infra notes / feasibility:
- Kernel slots: we can reserve the physical GPU slices for the 00:00-04:00 UTC window using a nightly affinity rule. That prevents noisy neighbors during their window.
- Prefetch and KV cache: recommend disabling aggressive prefetch for HealthSync jobs during the window to lower cold-start cost.
- Evictions: with the +20% headroom exception, we still need to allow preemption for high-priority prod traffic. I suggest the following enforcement: if preemption occurs during the window we automatically roll HealthSync back to soft-handback and issue a transient credit (formula included).

Operational steps I propose:
1) Implement nightly affinity rule for 3 weeks (infra change)
2) Apply autoscale +20% headroom for 7 days starting Friday (shorter than their ask)
3) Schedule daily 15-min check-in Slack thread during the window with both HealthSync and our ops on-call
4) If utilization exceeds 85% of total capacity during window -> immediate rollback to soft-handback + email escalation to leadership

I attached ops-runbook-diff.txt with threshold numbers. Laura — can you confirm the credit formula for rollbacks (we should be explicit in the SOW amendment).

Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Agreed immediate plan:

- Grant autoscale +20% headroom for 7 days starting Friday.
- Implement Marcus's infra affinity rule and the prefetch disable for HealthSync test jobs.
- Activate the ops-runbook-diff thresholds and start a daily 15-min Slack check-in during the 00:00-04:00 UTC window.
- Billing: Laura to draft a one-paragraph SOW amendment that includes the provisional usage cap and the rollback credit formula.

Action owners / timeline:

- Kimberly: ops runbook change live + on-call hooks (ETA: Friday 10:00 UTC)
- Laura: billing paragraph & SOW amendment draft (ETA: Friday noon)
- Hannah: notify HealthSync and schedule daily check-in (ETA: today 18:00 PT)
